rationale: I went and looked at the thing. shots/mgr100a-wide.png, seed 42, day 6, 14:43, a clear midsummer afternoon: the town above the lane is dense and finished, and the bottom of the picture is a BLACK RECTANGLE. It is not a rendering bug, it is an omission with a comment on it - buildGrid's last clause reads `// below the lane: our own building, with the river slipping between its two halves` and then sets rows 79..87 to VOID, and drawGround's first line is `if (t === WALL || t === VOID) continue`. So 1107 cells, 9.1% of the grid, the NEAREST rows and therefore the largest ones on screen, have never been painted by anything. Measured on HEAD: on a 1600x950 desktop the band runs from project(60,79,0)[1] = 676.4 to sillTop() = 794.6 of a canvas H = 859 - 13.8% of the picture; on a 390x844 phone it is 536.2 to 700.5 of H = 757.25, 21.7%. That is the answer to 'what would most change a thirty-second look', and it is a SPATIAL answer, which is what this batch needs: mapFlat is two iterations from firing, the map has not moved since #87, and `structures` and `passages` have not moved once in the whole run. So this batch is RUNG 4b, and b100 is the bet: give the diorama its foreground. The rest balance the grid and are aimed at what the same screenshot shows: an evenly-lit town under a sky whose eleven cloud banks cast nothing on it (b102, Sky 11 back, and drawClouds is a sky-strip-only pass - grepped, confirmed), an evening that does not end (b101, People 10 back, c137: a dusk stayer is still walking the plaza at 03h on four seeds), a plaza whose paving is 400 identical setts (b103, Plaza 7 back, New CA, and `moss`/`weed`/`lichen` appear nowhere in the source), and one measured polish (b104, Street 6 back). Cost discipline, third pass running: every number a brief needs is IN the brief, and where I could not price something I have said so rather than inventing a target.

queue.brief: Give the diorama a foreground. Rows 79..87 of the grid - everything south of LN_WALK_S, the nine rows nearest the observer - are VOID, and drawGround skips VOID, so the bottom of every frame is unpainted canvas. buildGrid already says what belongs there: 'below the lane: our own building, with the river slipping between its two halves'. Build it, seen from ABOVE, as the sill implies: the roof of the block we are looking out over - pitches and ridges running along the lane, a leaded valley the rain runs down, chimneys, a dormer or skylight, moss on the north slope, the parapet and gutter at its lane edge. It is the largest-celled part of the picture and it should pick up the systems it already lives among: snowCover/snowAt whiten it, drawRoofRow's sun/cloud/warmth shading, wetF sheen, CHIMNEYS[]/drawSmoke(t) leaning windDir(), windowLit for anything glazed, MUR_ROOSTS or a landed bird on the ridge. This is the bet: a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. Take the swing.

While you are in there, EVE_SPOTS line 3463 gives the deck's far end exactly two stay:1 posts at x 126.5 and 124.5, and 19 of 33 concert evenings fill both - add a third at 122.5 so a full house on the bridge is three, and price a.listen (the bell hold, ~0.5 h) into a stayer's walk so it does not cost them the post.

queue.brief: The sky and the ground ignore each other. drawClouds() draws eleven hashed banks on a (simT + windX) drift, but it draws them in the SKY STRIP only - above hz, under the backdrop - and nothing they pass over is shaded: the town has no moving cloud shadow. shadowF()/shSpread()/shOffset() only soften every object's own shadow uniformly under a lid. Connect them: let the banks throw soft shadows that travel across the courtyard, the allotments, the plaza and the river with the wind, so that on a broken-cloud day the light MOVES over the town and a viewer sees weather passing rather than a dimmer switch. The wide shot is where this pays: it is the only change on this list that alters the whole picture at once.
queue.measured: Not measured, deliberately - I am not going to invent a coverage target. Grepped and confirmed on HEAD: `cloudShadow` and `shadeAt` do not exist; drawClouds' only geometry is at `hz`; shadowF() has 14 call sites and every one is an object's own shadow. Pick the intensity by looking at it, and report what you chose.
queue.successLooksLike: On a seed and day with cloudCover in the broken band, a filmstrip cropped to the courtyard lawn shows the light rising and falling as a bank crosses, and the same instants at cloudCover < 0.04 are IDENTICAL to HEAD. The shadow travels with windDir() and reverses with windSign.
queue.avoid: Deterministic only - hash and simT, no new R() draw. This is a live pass, not a cache rebuild: the ground cache is repainted on its own dirty flag and a per-frame truth on it belongs in a live overlay (drawLitPanes' idiom). Watch the frame cost - `frame-cost.mjs`, not `perf.mjs` - a full-frame per-pixel pass will not do; a handful of soft ellipses composited in one multiply will.

queue.brief: The plaza's paving is the largest uniform surface in the town and it does not age. Give it a per-cell rule: moss and grass creep into the joints between the setts where nobody walks, thickening through wet seasons and dying back in frost and drought, and worn away where feet actually go. The courtyard already has this idea in `trod[]`/`wear[]` and litter, and the plaza has `pavingAt(x,y)` as its one paving predicate - this is that idea, on the other room, as a CA. New CA has four entries in 99 iterations and none of them are here; it is the town's signature kind and the plaza is its emptiest cell.
queue.measured: Grepped on HEAD: `moss`, `weed` and `lichen` appear nowhere in courtyard.html. `trod[]` and `litter[]` are courtyard-only. Nothing greens paving anywhere in the town.
queue.successLooksLike: Two shots of the plaza a season apart, warped from the same start, show visibly more green in the joints after a wet autumn than at the end of a dry summer, and the roundel's walked rings and the bench approaches stay clean. `tileKinds` or the census's green count moves.
queue.avoid: Per-cell variance at the grain the region is addressed by - a scalar that can reach zero needs `hash(x, y+k) > c`, not a global multiply, or the whole plaza flickers as one. It is cached ground: set the dirty flag on the cadence the growth actually changes, not per frame (`ground-rebuilds.mjs`). Do not make it walkable-different: nobody's route changes.
